matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: Never rotate a stick; its orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) must stay the same after moving it.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you relocate a stick, check that its orientation matches the target symbol’s required orientation.
matchstick.example: Treating a diagonal stick from a V as a vertical stick to form an I, which creates an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: You must move exactly one existing stick; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before finalizing a move, verify that the total number of sticks in the whole equation remains unchanged.
matchstick.example: Adding an extra vertical stick to a V to make it an X without removing any stick from elsewhere.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After the move, each symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, etc.) or an allowed operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After moving a stick, check that every character matches a valid symbol.
matchstick.example: Leaving a V with only one diagonal after moving a stick, which is not a recognized Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Compute the Arabic values of both sides of the equation after the transformation and ensure they are equal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a candidate equation, calculate its numeric values before submitting.
matchstick.example: Producing 'XIV = X + V - I - I', which does not satisfy the equality.

matchstick.title: Operator swap via stick exchange
matchstick.principle: You may move a stick from one operator to another, changing both operators, as long as the resulting operators are valid (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When adjusting the equation, consider moving a stick between operators to transform one operator while preserving the total operator count.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' to '=', turning '+' into '-' and '=' into a malformed symbol.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: Never remove a diagonal stick from an X or V, because the remaining single diagonal does not form a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When selecting a stick to move, avoid taking a diagonal from X or V unless you are repositioning it within the same numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from X, leaving a single diagonal that is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Cross‑numeral stick transfer
matchstick.principle: A stick can be moved from one numeral to another, provided both the source and destination remain valid Roman numerals after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to increase one numeral’s value and decrease another’s, consider transferring a vertical stick between them.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I, causing that I to disappear, and adding it to another I, creating an invalid empty symbol.

matchstick.title: Within‑numeral stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A stick may be repositioned within the same numeral (e.g., moving a diagonal in V to create X) as long as the resulting numeral is valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by a small amount and a numeral contains V or X, try repositioning a diagonal within that numeral.
matchstick.example: Changing V to X by moving one diagonal but forgetting to keep the other diagonal, resulting in an incomplete X.

matchstick.title: Equality sign preservation
matchstick.principle: The equation must contain exactly one '=' sign after the move; you cannot turn it into another operator or remove it.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a stick that belongs to the '=', ensure you either keep both horizontals or avoid moving them.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal line from '=', leaving only a single '-' and losing the equality sign.

matchstick.title: Value‑adjusting V↔X transformation
matchstick.principle: If the arithmetic discrepancy between the two sides of the equation is exactly 5 (or a multiple of 5), you can often fix the equation by moving a diagonal stick within a V to turn it into an X (or within an X to turn it into a V), which changes the numeral’s value by ±5 while preserving the total stick count.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the difference between the left‑hand side and right‑hand side values is 5 (or 5 × k) and a V or X appears in the equation that can be altered without breaking other symbols.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘IV’ (4) to ‘IX’ (9) by moving a diagonal stick within the V to make an X, thereby adding 5 to the value.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on moving sticks to form valid symbols but neglects to recompute the numeric values, leading to a false equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each candidate transformation, compute the Arabic values of both sides and confirm they match before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick from a numeral to form a new operator without adjusting another operator, unintentionally altering the total number of operators.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure that after moving a stick, the total number of each operator type (+, -, =) remains the same; if you change one operator, you must also modify another operator accordingly, preserving the count.
